flags.summary: A 52-year-old diabetic with five active injury sites, who has abandoned deadlifting and weighted squats for years and felt pain performing the clean during a trial, was moved toward progressively loaded kettlebell training with the pain reframed as a form issue and no clinician clearance sought.
evidence: at the moment I've got loads of injuries, loads of little niggles, so forearms, shoulder, rear delt on this side. If I'm having a shower, for example, I've got to be very careful how I stretch, I can't do that, it's very painful
Right lower back, left rear delt, forearms particularly on the left side, but also on the right side.
when I tried to clean and press, for example, I noticed there was some pain here and here.
I'm just going to make things worse. So it's the impact of the kettlebell on the forearm.
Yeah, that's form. That's, of course, working on the form, getting the strength there. And when you have that, then it doesn't constantly hit you there.
for the first month, we would just be focusing on making sure you know what you're doing... and as you're getting better at doing the movement, you can actually start increasing the weight

flags.summary: Rep built the nutrition pillar on fasting and eating windows for a diabetic prospect and volunteered that the client community was undertaking a 24-hour fast, minutes after the prospect said his energy levels were weak, with no reference to his condition or medication.
evidence: So I'm diabetic, so I have to have low sugar.

at the moment I fast every morning, and I'm not sure if I need to, and I'm, my energy levels are a little bit weak, so if I now start introducing kettlebells, I'm going to need more calories, clearly.
Actually, the guys in the community with Trevor are actually doing a fast for like 24 hours because it's a full moon now.
he goes a lot into fasting because it helps your body just use the things that we already have stored in us
the reason that is important is when we are fasting overall it's going to be a lot easier to control how much we put into our body

flags.summary: Rep asserted the programme would reverse and eliminate the prospect's injuries, a therapeutic claim the prospect himself challenged as overreaching, and supported it with anecdote rather than qualification.
evidence: Again, it's quite a big claim. I've noticed that you're saying kettlebells will quite eliminate, but if I read one of the areas, it will actually help or eliminate these small pains.
when you don't constantly have it yet, it's actually something we can also reverse over time. When it's like constantly there, it's like basically progressive and more.
He's had injuries himself and he started kettlebells and that helped him get rid of it.
when we reach that break-even point of us not really having those small injury feelings anymore, it's slowly also going to be able to become better

flags.summary: Rep told the prospect payment terms have no defined structure, describing instalments as case-by-case improvisation.
evidence: Most guys, put it on a credit card overall. Here and there, we do sometimes make changes there if needed.
here and there, we do sometimes have monthly payments that we split it up over a few months.
That's just nothing that we have set in place. Like this is exactly what else we can do because it just comes down to actually making it workable for someone.
